A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ensembling Sparse Autoencoders by the same authors. Their methods, experiments, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE training experiments, intrinsic evaluations, concept-detection accuracy, spurious-correlation removal results, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds expanded-SAE comparisons, automated interpretability assessments, further downstream evaluations, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: Naive bagging still averages independently initialized SAEs trained on the same data; boosting still trains sequentially on residuals and sums reconstructions. Feature concatenation and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures. The expanded SAE is a new comparator, not a modification of the proposed methods.

E1.justification: v2 adds automated feature interpretation, RAVEL attribute-value disentanglement, targeted probe perturbation, and spelling-related feature-absorption evaluations. It removes Amazon Review product-category prediction while retaining sentiment, programming-language, news-topic, document-language, and gender-debiasing tasks. These additions substantially broaden evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 introduces an expanded single-SAE comparator with the ensemble's feature count throughout the main evaluations and relevant appendix comparisons. The original smaller single SAE remains as the base SAE in Appendix D and other supplementary comparisons; it was not simply removed or renamed into the expanded baseline.

E3.justification: New controls match feature count and target boosting's aggregate L0, rather than comparing only against a smaller SAE. v2 removes relative sparsity and cosine-diversity metrics, adds AutoInterp, additional SAEBench and timing protocols, and introduces top-2 feature probing. It also evaluates retained downstream tasks with Pythia-160M and Gemma 2-2B configurations; original training-token budgets and the intrinsic test split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds first-versus-last SAE concept case studies investigating feature specificity and a top-2 feature-selection analysis. It adds expanded-SAE controls to the existing top-5 probing and SCR feature-ablation analyses. Conversely, v1's Appendix E diversity-threshold sensitivity study is removed; ensemble-size and hyperparameter sweeps remain.

E5.justification: The established reporting of means and 95% confidence intervals across five runs remains. v2 clarifies how individual runs serve as references for stability estimation and adds inference-time means and 95% intervals across ten batches in Supplementary Table 15. This does not establish an increase in training-run counts.

E6.justification: Shared ensemble scores are retained: Gemma boosting MSE remains 46.538, for example. v2 adds expanded-baseline results, including Gemma MSE 472.330, plus AutoInterp, top-2 probing, further model-specific downstream results, SAEBench scores, and timing measurements. New findings include expanded SAEs outperforming ensembles on TPP for Pythia-160M and Gemma 2-2B. Category-prediction, relative-sparsity, and diversity result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The bagging proposition receives a substantive but localized revision: v1's strong-law/almost-sure argument becomes a direct 1/J variance calculation in Proposition A.2, with a changed finiteness condition and removal of the almost-sure qualifier. Remark 3.2 also corrects weight absorption from Wenc to Wdec. The feature-concatenation and boosting results otherwise remain.

C1.justification: v2 strengthens the central empirical comparison from a smaller single SAE to an expanded SAE with matching feature count. The introduction replaces the prominently stated feature-diversity benefit with a claim of more interpretable features. These change the scope of the claimed advantages, while the bagging, boosting, and concatenation contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 newly argues that aggregate L0 is an unreliable interpretability proxy for ensembles and interprets the expanded baseline through a stability-reconstruction tradeoff. It develops guidance for single-feature versus multiple-feature concept detection and discusses negative Gemma SCR scores, TPP shortcomings, and applicability restrictions for absorption and unlearning evaluations. Earlier computational-cost and feature-redundancy limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplements the existing implementation recipe with Pythia-70M hyperparameters, expanded-baseline sparsity targeting, additional training times, and inference-timing hardware and procedures. It identifies default SAEBench settings and states that implementation code was submitted as supplementary material; the PDFs do not establish a public code release. Existing framework, hardware, and batch-size disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused distinctions from Switch SAEs, SAE Boost, and MP-SAEs, plus references supporting AutoInterp, specialized SAEs, and interpretability limitations. It removes the SAE-stitching discussion and the strong-law reference. These update neighboring-work positioning while preserving the overall relationship to classical ensembles and SAE variability.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much methodological exposition remain. v2 revises the abstract and experimental narrative around expanded baselines, renames Preliminaries to Formalizing SAE Ensembles, distinguishes base from expanded SAEs, and reorganizes appendices. It also adds impact and acknowledgment sections; these are targeted structural and language revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column conference layout, original base comparisons move into the appendix, and new qualitative, interpretability, downstream, and timing tables substantially restructure presentation. Intrinsic figures shrink from six panels to four, and diversity-threshold figures disappear. Revised Supplementary Figure 3 incorrectly labels the MSE panel as Relative Sparsity and the connectivity panel as MSE.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses a central weakness of v1: ensembles were compared only with a much smaller SAE. The expanded comparator, with matching feature count and sparsity targeted to boosting, substantially strengthens validation. Direct interpretability assessments and broader downstream tests provide additional evidence, including exceptions to ensemble superiority. Removing category/diversity analyses and introducing mislabeled plot axes are drawbacks, but the stronger comparisons and more informative evaluation outweigh them.
